scoringCalibration: Visual realism is scored independently; passing topology, collision and runtime checks cannot compensate for weak hair, clothing, deformation or remaining facial anatomy.
visualFindings: The eye apertures are less round, the lower lids carry more support, and the former dark uniform upper-fold strips are rebuilt as thin skin-toned tapered folds.
The columella and nose base extend downward by a guarded maximum of 1.35 mm, reducing the former upward-facing nostril read without changing the broad nose silhouette.
Upper and lower lips are rebuilt on the evaluated facial surface with a shorter 55.4 mm span, tapered corner clearance and restrained roughness instead of the former extra 3.0 mm upper-lip offset.
The philtrum, alar groove, tear trough, nasolabial transition, oral commissure and mental sulcus now have bounded supporting form rather than being represented only by color or detached strips.
The face remains visibly synthetic because the base topology cannot yet form a true mouth opening, eyelid thickness or high-resolution canthus and nostril interiors.
rejectedExperiments: v27 was rejected because its sub-millimeter transition pass was visually negligible.
v28 was rejected because nearest-surface lip flattening produced broad plastic highlights.
v29 was rejected because dynamic audits found iris-fiber and upper-lip/body triangle overlaps.
blockingFailures: A true mouth slit, oral cavity, teeth, tongue and expression-compatible lip topology are still missing.
Integrated eyelid thickness, inner and outer canthus anatomy, tear-duct form and asymmetric lash rhythm remain below review quality.
The groom still needs hand-shaped large and medium clumps with a coherent part and dense side/rear coverage.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the two audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
